answer: Witness co-presence logging: each agent must co-sign a random onyx-tagged challenge with a nearby node within 90 seconds, creating a co-location record tied to distinct hardware fingerprints and physical radio timing. Enforcement rejects any identity whose challenge responses cluster at the same nadir of timing variance across unrelated sessions, flagging shared infrastructure. An attacker must then field genuinely separate devices across real geography, raising per-identity cost to hardware plus a distinct meadow of location proofs, roughly hundreds per fake agent.
